title: Eugenio Chacarra comments on his chances of winning the Race to Dubai after Rory McIlroy's poor third round

 Featured Golf Eugenio Chacarra comments on his chances of winning the Race to Dubai after Rory McIlroy’s poor third round
 Antony Martin Sat 14 November 2026 13:03, UK Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images Follow us on Google Discover Eugenio Chacarra is currently sitting in a tie for fourth alongside Rory McIlroy with just one round remaining in Dubai. 
 Chacarra posted a third round score of 68 on Saturday at the DP World Tour Championship, while McIlroy labored to a very ordinary 72.
 For golf fans watching at home, things could not be set up more perfectly heading into the final round on Sunday.
 Chacarra knows that he only has to finish ahead of McIlroy and Jon Rahm in order to clinch the season-long Race to Dubai title.
 Who will win the Race to Dubai title?
 Rory McIlroy and Patrick Reed are trying to catch Eugenio Chacarra
 4 comments Comment Like or Comment Have your say Sign-in now for free Meanwhile, the Northern Irishman has to finish higher than the Spaniard, and no worse than fourth outright.
 There is obviously a lot of golf left to be played, and McIlroy will undoubtedly still be very confident in his chances of winning the Race to Dubai, especially given the experience he has.
 However, Chacarra is certainly not short of confidence either, and on Saturday afternoon, he spoke about his hopes of being crowned the season-long champion.
 Eugenio Chacarra on his chances of beating Rory McIlroy to the Race to Dubai title
 Chacarra spoke to reporters after his third round in Dubai on Saturday, and he was asked how he feels about his chances of winning the Race to Dubai on Sunday.
 MORE RORY MCILROY STORIES “ Yeah, I mean, I just want to win the tournament. I’m not far away. I think I’m three shots out now. Hopefully they don’t make a lot of birdies coming in and I have a shot tomorrow. I know if I win the tournament, I win the ranking, “ the Spaniard replied.
 “ So that’s what I wanted to do in Abu Dhabi and I want to do it here. That’s what we prepare for and I’m going to have a chance on Sunday. That’s what we dream of since I was little is to win big events on Sunday, and I’m going to have a chance.
 “ I’m ready. I love the game of golf. I love practising. I work so hard for these moments, and I’m going to go out there and enjoy it.
 “ I think all of my goals have been done this season. So I’m just playing free. This is an extra bonus to have a chance to win it, and just to enjoy every moment. Like you said, not a lot of people can enjoy this moment and have a chance to win The Race to Dubai. So I’m going to have a chance tomorrow, and I’m going to go try and enjoy it as much as possible. “ 
 All that remains to be seen now is whether Eugenio Chacarra is able to hold off Rory McIlroy on Sunday in order to win his first ever Race to Dubai crown.
